question:
A customer reports a defect in the executable we shipped to them two years ago, and to investigate it we need that very same executable back, byte for byte, but the toolchain and third-party libraries on our machines have been upgraded since then. What should the team have been tracking and preserving so that this would be possible?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
[JEV filter] kept 10 of 10 guidelines (JEV 'lenient' score > 0.5)

# Guidelines
- Place all source code under version control (a source code version control system) so that the exact version shipped to any customer can be retrieved. Version control tools allow tracking and documenting changes to source code in a single repository, and changes can be discarded or a previous baseline restored when needed. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Change Management and Version Control/Source Code Version Control and Management.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Identify and control all Software Configuration Items (SCIs) — not just source code, but every item that contributes to the delivered product — so that the full configuration of any release is known and can be reconstructed. [SWEBOK excerpt e412eff79e6ccfe4f324], and a CI is an item or aggregation [SWEBOK excerpt 875b905f12990583528e]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Item Definition and Management.md; root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/SCM Audits and Configuration Identification/Software Configuration Identification and Item Control.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Place the build toolchain (including compilers and other supporting tools) and build instructions under SCM control. [SWEBOK excerpt 9e95c89fd76e71157968]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Build Tools and Version Control Management.md; root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/In-Process Audits and Software Release Management.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Ensure SCM is capable of reproducing previous [SWEBOK excerpt 28558659431243b1fdfe], which must therefore also be preserved under SCM control. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/In-Process Audits and Software Release Management.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Produce and retain a Version Description Document (VDD) for each release. [SWEBOK excerpt 70d681ad63533bb123da] and selects the correct variants of those items; [SWEBOK excerpt 7ea550447dc0afcc450c]). (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md) [JEV 0.86]
- Maintain a software library (binary repository) that stores the built artifacts from each release, so that previously built executables can be retrieved and redeployed without needing to rebuild. A repository stores binaries [SWEBOK excerpt 4ccb31704d1b97218915]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management System Tools and Components.md; root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/In-Process Audits and Software Release Management.md) [JEV 0.93]
- Produce and preserve a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for each build. [SWEBOK excerpt 450578f233490c4cd9fa], capturing what exactly went into the build. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Software Build Artifacts and Continuous Integration Processes.md) [JEV 0.91]
- Retain build outputs as quality, security, or compliance records. [SWEBOK excerpt 72f5358c04de49c9134c] and [SWEBOK excerpt a4ef685722d26ada8f79]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Build Process Quality Verification and Documentation.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Implement release management practices that identify, package, and track the contents of each customer delivery, including release notes describing platform requirements, and optionally a digital signature or integrity hash to verify the released item. [SWEBOK excerpt e8f6a76a50aac203ea7a]), and [SWEBOK excerpt e4b18c7772a0f7814195]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Release Management Tools and Documentation Requirements.md; root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Maintain integrity indicators (such as SHA1, MD5, or MAC) for all configuration items and released artifacts as part of Configuration Status Accounting. Modern SCM includes indicators of integrity (e.g., MAC, SHA1, MD5) so that the authenticity and unchanged state of preserved artifacts can be verified later. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Configuration Status Accounting and Reporting/Software Configuration Status Reporting and Auditing.md) [JEV 0.94]
